key_takeaways: Out-of-pocket payments made up 71.9 percent of current health spending in 2023.{{health_system.financing:3}}
Practicing doctors fell 16.9 percent to about 55,000 in 2025, largely because of emigration.{{health_system.workforce:3}}

Communicable, maternal, prenatal and nutritional conditions caused 63.7 percent of deaths in 2021, and noncommunicable diseases 27.7 percent.{{country_overview.disease_prevalence:1}}{{country_overview.disease_prevalence:2}}
Health insurance enrollment passed 23 million in September 2026, roughly 10 percent of the 2025 population.{{health_system.public_system:7}}{{health_system.public_system:4}}
health_system: Health spending was 4.19 percent of GDP in 2023, below Kenya, Egypt and South Africa.{{health_system.financing:1}}{{health_system.financing:7}}
Of 40,368 hospitals and clinics counted in mid-2021, 85.2 percent were primary and only 0.4 percent tertiary.{{health_system.public_system:1}}
The United States intends to provide $2.1 billion over five years under a December 2025 health memorandum.{{health_system.financing:11}}
market: Evercare built the 165-bed Evercare Hospital Lekki in Lagos, and Padiyath Healthcare is building a 300-bed hospital in Abuja.{{health_system.competitive_landscape:1}}{{health_system.competitive_landscape:3}}
UVA Health supports the kidney transplant program at Federal Medical Centre Umuahia, one of several active U.S. academic ties.{{health_system.competitive_landscape:5}}
Central Bank data show $549 million of health travel spending in the first nine months of 2025, up 18 percent.{{health_system.competitive_landscape:11}}
risks: Presidential and National Assembly elections on 16 January 2027 could change federal priorities.{{country_overview.government:4}}
In 2024, 4,193 doctors and dentists emigrated, and 72.9 percent of surveyed medical and nursing students intended to practice abroad.{{health_system.workforce:3}}{{health_system.education:1}}
The 2026 budget proposal gave health N2.48 trillion (US$1.86 billion), about 4.2 percent, below the Abuja Declaration's 15 percent target.{{health_system.financing:8}}{{health_system.financing:10}}

recent.text: The IFC and NSIA financed MedServe's $154.1 million project for diagnostic, radiotherapy and cardiac catheterization centers.{{recent_developments.2:1}}
Health insurance enrollment reached 22.03 million, up 35 percent in a year, as mandatory provisions are phased in.{{recent_developments.1:1}}
Nigeria confirmed an imported Ebola Bundibugyo case in Abuja, and 44 contacts are being monitored.{{recent_developments.0:1}}{{recent_developments.0:2}}

country_background: Nigeria, a federal presidential republic of 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory, Abuja, had about 237.5 million people in 2025.{{country_overview.demographics:5}}{{country_overview.demographics:6}}{{country_overview.government:1}}{{country_overview.government:2}}{{country_overview.demographics:1}} Bola Tinubu has been president since 29 May 2023, and Muhammad Ali Pate is Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare.{{country_overview.government:2}}{{country_overview.government:3}}{{country_overview.government:5}}{{country_overview.government:7}} The federal government sets regulation, while states and local governments run general hospitals and primary health care centers.{{country_overview.government:6}} Real GDP grew 4.2 percent in the first half of 2026, and inflation eased to 14.63 percent in September 2026.{{country_overview.economy:1}}{{country_overview.economy:6}} The population is young, with 40.5 percent under 15, and life expectancy at birth was 54.6 years in 2024.{{country_overview.demographics:12}}{{country_overview.demographics:10}} The key risk is affordability: an estimated 69.6 percent of Nigerians lived below $4.20 a day in 2025, and households paid most health costs.{{country_overview.economy:1}}{{health_system.financing:3}}
